chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever finds wealth or a camel in a wilderness from the earth which was exhausted and its owner had abandoned from what he did not pursue it, so someone else finds it and stands to look after it and spends expenditure until he revives it from the exhaustion and from the death, so it is for him, and there is no way for him (the previous owner) upon it. But rather it is like the ownerless thing.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for finding abandoned property in barren land?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of 'ihya' al-mawat' (reviving dead land/property), establishing that a finder who expends effort to revive an abandoned asset in barren land acquires full ownership (milkiyyah) without owing compensation to the original owner. It highlights the Shia juristic view that abandonment combined with the finder's labor transforms the asset into a free resource, akin to unclaimed goods, emphasizing the value of productive effort in Islamic economic law.
